text:
devon: alerting — we're seeing a sudden ECC / Xid error spike across west-2 GPU pool, capacity reported down ~18%. Not a single rack, looks distributed. Anyone else seeing this?
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-error-rate-high — west-2-gpu-pool — error_rate=12% over 5m, impacted_capacity=18% — incident=INC-2024-4821
sam: on it. pulling node lists and recent reboots. can someone post a quick nvidia-smi / dmesg sample from affected hosts?
alexa: grabbed one host (gpu-node-23). nvidia-smi shows some ECC errors, small bit flips. output: `GPU 0: ECC errors corrected=124, uncorrected=0`
alexa: dmesg shows repeating: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID: 1421` — lots of Xid 13s.
jamal: Xid 13 usually bus/firmware issues or driver/kernel mismatch. Which driver/kernel?
alexa: kernel 6.1.12, nvidia 530.41.03 (same as last week). no recent kernel upgrades in the pool.
maria: curious if this correlates with any maintenance or power events in the rack-level telemetry. storage/thermal?
devon: infra metrics show slight temp rise on a subset of hosts ~2C over the last 12h, not huge. network flaps? nothing flagged.
sam: I'm going to start a controlled drain of the worst 6 nodes (highest Xid counts) and mark them for replacement. plan: `kubectl drain gpu-node-{23,27,45,62,71,89} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then move workloads to other regions. Thoughts?
jamal: +1 to drain. but we should throttle drains to avoid too much cross-region egress. do in two batches. also bump fallback policy to allow CPU-backed replicas temporarily.
alexa: compiling failing job logs to a gist for postmortem. snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID: 9999
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus: GPU 0000:65:00.0
```
ops-bot: [ACTION] paging oncall (sam) — oncall@pagerduty
devon: can we snapshot ECC counters across the fleet and run a query to find nodes with >100 corrected ECC in 24h? that'll help prioritize.
sam: running query now. expected output: `SELECT node, sum(ecc_corrected) FROM gpu_metrics WHERE ts > now() - 24h GROUP BY node ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 50`
maria: also add `dmesg | grep -i xid` to the diagnostics bundle.
jamal: check BIOS/firmware versions too. some vendors had a bad firmware that surfaced under load.
alexa: I found 3 nodes with GPU firmware mismatch to rest of fleet. marking them.
devon: operational decision: drain first batch (23,27,45) now, second batch (62,71,89) in 20m if metrics don't stabilize. rolling replacements scheduled with provider — RMA for suspected flaky cards.
sam: executing drain batch 1 now. I'll watch autoscaler to ensure we don't starve production.
alexa: drain logs: `evicting pod abc-123, evicting pod xyz-456` — looks clean.
ops-bot: [NOTIFY] routing policy updated: route >75% of new GPU requests for latency-critical customers to east-1 for next 1h.
maria: cost note — cross-region shift will increase egress and infra cost. calling this out for finance postmortem.
devon: update: after batch 1 drain, error-rate dropped from 12% -> 7% in 10m. still above baseline.
jamal: expected. keep going with batch 2. also queue firmware update for matched nodes if vendor confirms fix.
sam: starting batch 2 drain now.
alexa: after batch 2, corrected ECC counters still climbing on 4 remaining nodes; two of them report intermittent Xid 79 (GPU fallen off bus). those two will be taken offline immediately.
devon: capacity impact now 9% and trending down. opening incident board SOC-INC-4821 and assigning roles: responder=sam, lead=devon, infra-contact=maria, vendor-liaison=jamal.
ops-bot: [UPDATE] incident SOC-INC-4821 created — timeline tracking enabled.
maria: vendor support responding; they asked for `lspci -vvv` and `flashrom -i` outputs. jamal, can you handle?
jamal: on it. collecting and uploading to vendor share.
alexa: adding logs + per-pod failure traces to the incident doc. also pinned a few reproducible jobs that hit GPU-fatal errors.
sam: summary for now: draining and replacing flaky cards is reducing error rate and restoring capacity. short-term mitigation: gradual routing shift to east-1 and allow CPU fallback for non-latency critical workloads. long-term: fleet-wide firmware audit and scheduled remediations.
devon: thanks team. I'll post a short blameless RCA draft after vendor analysis. please drop any lingering notes here. :thumbsup:
maria: noted cost impact and will add to incident finances.
ops-bot: [RESOLVE] temporary routing policy expires in 55m unless extended.
alexa: small follow-up — let's add ECC corrected counters to our alerting rate to catch earlier next time.
jamal: agreed. create a PR against alerts repo? I'll start it.
sam: closing thread for daily ops; will reopen if the vendor finds anything critical.
devon: closing — keep monitoring.
